theory.intro: The **instantaneous rate of change** of $f(x)$ at $x = a$ is the rate at that single moment. It is the gradient of the **tangent** to the curve at $(a, f(a))$, written $f'(a)$.
facts: The instantaneous rate of change at $x = a$ is written $f'(a)$, read "$f$ prime of $a$".
As the second point of a secant slides towards $a$, the secant turns until it becomes the tangent.
A tangent sloping upwards means the instantaneous rate is positive, $f'(a) > 0$.
A horizontal tangent means $f'(a) = 0$, which is a stationary point.
A tangent sloping downwards means the instantaneous rate is negative, $f'(a) < 0$.
steps: Identify the point of interest $(a, f(a))$ on the curve.
Recognise that the instantaneous rate is the gradient of the tangent line at that single point.
Determine whether the tangent slopes upward ($f' > 0$), is horizontal ($f' = 0$), or slopes downward ($f' < 0$).
Interpret the value of $f'(a)$ in context with appropriate rate units.

foundation.solution_text:
$L_1\text{ cuts the curve at two distinct points, so it is a secant line (average rate).}$
$L_2\text{ touches the curve at the single point } P\text{, so it is the tangent line (instantaneous rate).}$

$\text{At } A\text{, the tangent slopes upward to the right, so } f'(x) > 0\text{ (positive).}$
$\text{At } B\text{, the tangent is horizontal, so } f'(x) = 0\text{ (zero).}$
$\text{At } C\text{, the tangent slopes downward to the right, so } f'(x) < 0\text{ (negative).}$

foundation.question_text:
A vehicle's speedometer reads $75\text{ km/h}$ at the exact moment $t = 12\text{ s}$.
State whether this speedometer reading represents an average speed or an instantaneous speed.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{The speedometer measures the speed of the vehicle at that single precise moment in time.}$
$\text{The speedometer reading represents an instantaneous speed (gradient of the tangent).}$

foundation.question_text: Explain how the gradient of a secant line between $(a, f(a))$ and $(a+h, f(a+h))$ relates to the gradient of the tangent at $x = a$ as $h$ approaches zero.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{As } h \to 0\text{, the second point approaches } (a, f(a)).$
$\text{The secant line rotates until it coincides with the tangent line at } x = a.$
$\text{Therefore, the limiting value of the secant gradient is the tangent gradient } f'(a).$

foundation.question_text:
Classify each statement as describing either an average rate or an instantaneous rate:
1. A car travelled $150\text{ km}$ in $2\text{ hours}$, averaging $75\text{ km/h}$.
2. A police radar clocking a motorcycle at $110\text{ km/h}$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Statement 1 describes an average rate (calculated over a } 2\text{-hour interval).}$
$\text{Statement 2 describes an instantaneous rate (measured at a single specific instant).}$

foundation.question_text:
The graph of $y = f(x)$ has a turning point (local maximum) at $(3, 8)$.
State the value of $f'(3)$ and describe the geometric appearance of the tangent line at this point.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{At a smooth turning point, the tangent line is horizontal.}$
$\text{A horizontal line has a gradient of } 0.$
$f'(3) = 0$

foundation.question_text:
A cup of coffee cools on a desk.
The temperature graph is steep at first and becomes flatter as it approaches room temperature.
Explain what is happening to the instantaneous rate of cooling over time.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{The tangent line to the temperature curve becomes less steep (closer to horizontal) as time passes.}$
$\text{This means the instantaneous rate of cooling decreases in magnitude over time as the temperature nears room temperature.}$

development.question_text:
Secant gradients for $f(x) = x^2 + x$ on intervals $[2, 2+h]$ are evaluated as follows:
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} h & 1 & 0.1 & 0.01 & 0.001 \\ \hline m_{\text{secant}} & 6 & 5.1 & 5.01 & 5.001 \end{array}$
Deduce the exact value of the instantaneous rate of change $f'(2)$.
development.solution_text:
$\text{As } h \to 0\text{, the secant gradients approach the value } 5.$
$\text{Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at } x = 2\text{ is } f'(2) = 5.$

development.question_text:
A skydiver falls until reaching terminal velocity.
On their velocity–time graph, the curve flattens into a horizontal line at $v = 55\text{ m/s}$.
Interpret what happens to the skydiver's instantaneous acceleration (rate of change of velocity) at terminal velocity.
development.solution_text:
$\text{At terminal velocity, the velocity graph is horizontal, so the gradient of the tangent is } 0.$
$\text{The instantaneous acceleration is } 0\text{ m/s}^2\text{, meaning the skydiver falls at constant speed.}$

development.question_text:
A commuter travels $60\text{ km}$ in $1\text{ hour}$, so their average speed is $60\text{ km/h}$.
However, at $t = 30\text{ min}$, their speedometer showed $95\text{ km/h}$.
Explain how both statements can be correct simultaneously.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Average speed is calculated across the entire } 1\text{-hour journey } (60\text{ km/h}),\text{ accounting for stops.}$
$\text{Instantaneous speed } (95\text{ km/h})\text{ is the gradient of the tangent at that specific moment.}$
$\text{A vehicle's instantaneous speed can exceed its overall average speed during open road segments.}$

development.question_text:
For $f(x) = 2x^2$, find the gradient of the secant line over $[3, 3.1]$ and over $[3, 3.01]$.
Use these to estimate the gradient of the tangent at $x = 3$.
development.solution_text:
$f(3) = 2(3^2) = 18$
$f(3.1) = 2(3.1^2) = 19.22 \implies \dfrac{19.22 - 18}{0.1} = 12.2$
$f(3.01) = 2(3.01^2) = 18.1202 \implies \dfrac{18.1202 - 18}{0.01} = 12.02$
$\text{As the interval shrinks, the secant gradients approach } 12.$
$\text{Estimated tangent gradient: } f'(3) = 12$

$\text{Point } D\text{ has the steepest negative slope.}$
$\text{Point } C\text{ has a moderate negative slope.}$
$\text{Point } B\text{ has a horizontal slope of } 0.$
$\text{Point } A\text{ has a steep positive slope.}$
$\text{Order from smallest to largest: } D < C < B < A$

mastery.question_text: For $f(x) = x^2$, algebraically find the secant gradient over $[x, x+h]$, and evaluate the limit as $h \to 0$ to find the general formula for the tangent gradient $f'(x)$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Secant gradient} = \dfrac{(x+h)^2 - x^2}{h}$
$= \dfrac{x^2 + 2xh + h^2 - x^2}{h}$
$= \dfrac{2xh + h^2}{h}$
$= 2x + h$
$\text{As } h \to 0, \text{ the limit is } f'(x) = 2x.$

mastery.question_text:
The graph of a polynomial function $y = f(x)$ has tangent slopes $f'(-2) = 3$, $f'(0) = 0$, and $f'(2) = -5$.
Describe the behaviour of the function at each of these three $x$-values.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{At } x = -2: f'(-2) = 3 > 0\text{, so the function is increasing (rising to the right).}$
$\text{At } x = 0: f'(0) = 0\text{, so the function has a stationary point (horizontal tangent).}$
$\text{At } x = 2: f'(2) = -5 < 0\text{, so the function is decreasing (falling to the right).}$

mastery.question_text:
In a chemical reaction, the mass of gas produced over $t$ minutes is $M(t)$.
The average rate of production over the first $10\text{ minutes}$ is $4\text{ g/min}$, but the initial instantaneous rate is $f'(0) = 12\text{ g/min}$.
Explain the physical reason for this difference.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{The reaction proceeds fastest at the start when reactant concentrations are highest } (f'(0) = 12\text{ g/min}).$
$\text{As reactants are consumed, the rate slows down steadily.}$
$\text{The average rate of } 4\text{ g/min}\text{ averages the fast initial burst with subsequent slower production.}$
